title: Summing Amplifier: Add Voltages at the Virtual Ground
topic: Summing amplifier: three input voltages drive a common inverting node through their own resistors; KCL at virtual ground yields V_out = -R_f·(V1/R1 + V2/R2 + V3/R3).

beats.narration: How do you add three voltages with one op-amp? It's easier than you think.

elements.content: Three voltages in, one weighted sum out.

beats.narration: Take the inverting op-amp and replace the single input resistor with three. Each input V k drives the same V minus node through its own R k. R f closes the feedback loop.

elements.content: Op-amp triangle pointing right, V+ on bottom tied to ground
Three input resistors R1, R2, R3 stacked on the left, all meeting at V-
R_f feedback resistor from V_out back to V-
three branches share one virtual-ground node

beats.narration: V minus is held at zero by the feedback. So each input contributes its own current — V k over R k — and they all converge at the same node. Their sum then flows through R f to V out.

elements.content: Three streams of charge dots through R1, R2, R3 converging at V-
Combined stream of charge dots through R_f to V_out

beats.narration: Kirchhoff's current law at V minus gives the punchline: V out equals minus R f times the sum of V k over R k. Each input is scaled by its own ratio.

elements.content: if R1 = R2 = R3 = R, it's just a (scaled) inverted sum

beats.narration: Feed in three sinewaves at different frequencies and the output traces their sum, inverted and scaled. That's an analog audio mixer in one chip.

elements.content: Three small sinusoidal V1, V2, V3 traces stacked on the left
V_out: inverted sum, larger and complex, on the right
one chip — an inverting analog mixer
